title: Consumption Atlas — Marginal Cost Waterfall and Export Wizard for Chat Flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Product and platform teams need a fast way to understand marginal token costs for multi-turn chat flows and to export role-aware, auditable breakdowns for chargeback and finance. Current console views show aggregate token spend but hide how costs accrue across turns, system/prompt vs user tokens, and pricing tiers. Goal: design a Consumption Atlas — a compact panel that surfaces a marginal-cost waterfall for a selected chat route, a timeline of per-turn attribution, and an export wizard that produces role-aware, signed CSV/JSONL/Parquet with applied rate-cards and SLA adjustments.
goals: Show marginal cost per chat turn and cumulative cost for a selected time window
Make attribution explicit by role (system, assistant, user, tool) and by model variant/quantization profile
Provide export presets for Finance (line-item CSV), Analytics (JSONL with token-level rows), and Compliance (signed Parquet with KMS metadata)
Include rate-card overlay so users can toggle price schedules and see forecasted spend
constraints: Must render within Console route panel without full page navigation
Maintain <150ms initial render for 20-row chat slices
Exports cannot include raw PII — must respect mask rules from data governance
decisions: Use a stacked marginal waterfall chart (per-turn delta stacked by role) instead of a per-token histogram to surface impact of single turns
Default time window: last 7 days; allow quick toggles for custom date ranges and sampling rate
Export wizard will include a preview mode that applies rate-card and shows estimated line totals before download
Permission gating: only users with 'billing:export' may produce role-aware exports; anonymized exports available to 'viewer' roles
feedback: PM (Marta Singh): prefer CSV preview with line counts and sample privacy redaction shown inline
Eng (Rajat Menon): concerns about initial render cost for large chat slices; suggested server-side aggregation and streaming preview
Security (Lina Gomez): flagged Parquet signed export for KMS header structure; needs SRE integration ticket
Finance (Oliver Beck): wants rate-card override tied to committed tier for Dedicated customers
acceptance_criteria: Atlas panel renders marginal waterfall for selected chat route and time window
Per-turn drilldown reveals role-level token counts and per-role cost contribution
Export wizard produces three preset formats (CSV, JSONL, Parquet) with correct rate-card application and a downloadable signed file for Parquet
Permission model prevents role-aware export for viewer-only users and shows anonymized preview instead
Performance: initial panel render for 20 chat turns under 150ms in staging telemetry

2025-03-18 — Updated acceptance criteria to include performance target and permission gating tests.
implementation_notes: Backend will expose /routes/{id}/consumption/aggregate?window=7d&sample=1 to return pre-aggregated per-turn deltas and role slices
Client will render waterfall using a canvas-backed microchart to meet render SLAs; animation optional behind feature flag
Export wizard UI will request a signed URL from the export service and show preview rows streamed back (first 100 rows) before confirming download
risks: Large historical routes may still exceed staging budgets; need sampling heuristics
Rate-card complexity: multiple active promotions and committed tiers could make live previews differ from final invoice — add explicit 'estimate' badge
PII leakage risk if export preview includes unredacted user messages; enforce governance mask before any preview

owner_notes: Primary focus is to make marginal costs explorable and exportable with clear guardrails. Keep the first iteration narrow (one route, 7d window, three export formats). We'll iterate to multi-route comparisons and longer retention once backend aggregation is stable.
